chapter: Road shows, carnivals and New York
title: A winter in New York: Stone, records, and Ralph Sutton
summary: Taylor took Punch to New York for the winter; he made records, played jam sessions and gigs with Sutton, and lost a chance with pianist Stone.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: What did he work with? His name's Stone. The last name is Stone. I can't think of his first name. What did he work with? I was to make piano, I was to make records with him, and the same show, see how I got to New York, when the carnival closed, Charlie Taylor was the man who had the brown mannequin. He said, Puncher, never lived in New York, no time, why don't you come on and go up there with me and stay with me, just you know, just winter, until I get ready for my show to go out and then we'd all come out together. Well I went on there with him, see, and that's when I went to playing them jam sessions, and making records, that's when I made them records, Ho Ho, Ho, Ho, and then. Yeah. That's the time I made them records, and I lived at his house in New York, so I got this fellow, Stone, I'll tell you about, I think his first name. He called me a pretty full time, told me when his job was going to start, when he was going to make records and everything, and Charlie Taylor got ready to go out on the road, well I just dropped all that, went on the road with Charlie Taylor, see, again. But I wish I would have stood there, if I stood there I would have stood there right, see. Stone, his name is some kind of Stone, he's a good piano player, good musician, he had a band in Chicago a while.
I can't think of who that would be. His name's Stone, anybody tell you.
Guy Kelly, and Red Carey, you heard of him, Carey, played saxophone. Red Carey? Yeah, you never heard of him either?
I can't place him, I'll play him.
Well they played with Stone band in Chicago, all them guys, he had a nice band there man. And then he left Chicago and went to New York see, and stood around they playing.
Who else did you play gigs with in New York?
Well just fellows, boy white boy played piano, was his name?
He made the records with you, is that the one?

Yeah. Ralph Sutton. Sutton, yeah. I played with him, tell the truth, the whole time I was in New York, because everything I got he called me up and I'd go on with him, even Harvard Connecticut and all out there I went with him.
